newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish tanker to begin loading Iraqi oil Monday.
newsitem.headline: Turkish tanker to begin loading Iraqi oil Monday.

text.p: Loading of the first tanker of Iraqi crude to be exported through Turkey in six years will begin Monday morning at the southern Turkish port of Ceyhan, Anatolian news agency said Sunday.
Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller are expected to jointly press the button to begin loading at a ceremony Monday morning, pipeline company BOTAS said Sunday.
The tanker is to transport crude to Turkey's state refiner Tupras' Aliaga refinery in the western city of Izmir.

Tupras has a contract with Iraq, approved by the United Nations, to buy 75,000 barrels per day under a U.N. deal that allows Iraq to sell crude in order to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies.
